ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, Sep. 7, 2001, as amended) Articles 5-2 through 5-5; Enforcement Decree thereof; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions (Act No. 5493, Jul. 3, 1997, as amended) Article 3; Regulations on Customer Identification and Verification and the Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information promulgated by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU). mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry, Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: original Court-issued certificate -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille -> destination state in Apostille Convention. Consular route for non-Apostille state: original Court-issued certificate -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular authentication -> legalization by the destination state's embassy or consulate in Korea. These routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service, District Tax Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: original Tax Office certificate -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille -> destination state. Consular route: original Tax Office certificate -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular authentication -> legalization by destination state's diplomatic agent in Korea. Parallel routes, never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certified Copy of the Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: South Korean Notary Public in the district where the registered office is located
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: Articles signed before notary -> notary certificate -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille -> destination state. Consular route: notary certificate -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular authentication -> destination state's embassy or consulate in Korea legalizes. Do not use both paths sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Incorporators Resolution appointing initial Manager and granting Power of Attorney for pre-incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All founding incorporators / initial managers of Yuhan Hoesa, signed in the presence of a notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: notarize signatures of all incorporators -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille -> destination state. Consular route: notarize signatures -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular authentication -> legalization by destination state's embassy/consulate in Korea. Parallel and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of material investor or foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: certificate from home registry -> Apostille issued by the home state's competent authority -> delivered directly to Korean bank or registry. Consular route: certificate -> home state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular authentication -> legalization by the Republic of Korea's embassy/consulate in that home state. These two routes are alternative and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank maintaining the corporate or investor account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: letter on bank letterhead signed by bank officer -> notarization of bank signature -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille -> destination state. Consular route: notarized bank signature -> Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular authentication -> destination state's consular legalization. Parallel routes only.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, incorporators, directors, senior managers, and authorized signatories must undergo dynamic automated and analyst-reviewed screening prior to authorization and on a rolling 48-hour basis against: (i) the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions lists; (ii) the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Consolidated Sanctions lists; (iii) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions target list; (iv) the UK OFSI consolidated list; (v) the Republic of Korea's own financial sanctions restrictions published by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Financial Services Commission, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit; and (vi) reputationally sourced adverse media, politically exposed persons databases, and enforcement action lists maintained by FATF-style regional bodies. Matching must use exact, fuzzy, phonetic, and transliteration algorithms covering Korean, Hanja-derived names, passports, dates of birth, and nationalities. Any PEP, PEP family member, or close associate triggers enhanced due diligence with documented source of wealth, source of funds, senior management approval, and annual re-validation; any hit for a sanctioned person or jurisdiction stops the formation process until legal counsel issues a clearance opinion or a license is obtained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-RO), online name search and registration database at iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name must be stated in Korean Hangul characters because the company registry records names in the Korean alphabet. A parallel English business name may be maintained for commercial use, but the statutory corporate name must end with 'Yuhan Hoesa' to denote a limited liability company. Foreign words may be transliterated phonetically into Hangul; direct Roman letters are not accepted as the sole registered name in the company registry except where expressly permitted by a ruling of the Supreme Court of Korea. Four-tier naming conventions are: (1) distinctive and non-deceptive main element; (2) descriptive element indicating the business purpose, such as 'Royalty Financing' or 'Digital Brand Funding'; (3) corporate form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'; and (4) optional parallel English or transliterated trade name filed as a supplementary business name in contracts, invoices, and marketing materials.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the registry office issues a written statement specifying the conflicting same-name marker, prohibited token, or non-compliant corporate form. The applicant or its attorney-in-fact must file a written objection with the head of the relevant District Court Registry within 14 days of receipt, citing the Korean Non-Contentious Civil Litigation Procedure Act and the Registration Reporter Regulation. The objection must propose a revised distinct trade name, attach a name availability report from the i-RO system, and explain why the rejected name is not identical or misleading. If the registry examiner maintains the rejection, an immediate request for adjudication may be filed with the High Court within 14 days, and thereafter a final appeal to the Supreme Court within 14 days. Concurrently, a fresh name reservation may be filed using a second-choice name to avoid delay, and legal counsel must issue a written clearance opinion before any final execution.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox, without a dedicated physical suite, lease, and full-time or part-time managerial presence, is commercially and administratively rejected for a revenue-based financing fund in the Republic of Korea. The National Tax Service requires an actual business place for business registration and will refuse a P.O. box or virtual-only address; the courts registry will likewise require a domestic physical seat for Yuhan Hoesa; and Korean banks, operating under the Financial Services Commission's customer due diligence rules, will refuse to open an operating account for a company whose registered office cannot accommodate service of process, record keeping, or on-site inspections. A premium serviced office with dedicated desks, signage, meeting rooms, telephone answering, and a one-year lease may be accepted if the company actually uses it and keeps records there. However, for the financing industry, a serviced office alone is still a yellow flag; the safer strategy is a physical office in Seoul or another major city with at least one resident non-executive manager and a clearly identified compliance officer.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months: approximately 5% for a genuine physical office with lease and staff; 15% for a fully serviced office with a management agreement and staff presence; 45% for a virtual office or shared mailbox. Required checklist for surviving inspection: (1) exterior signage and building directory listing Yuhan Hoesa; (2) lease agreement in Korean with term of at least one year; (3) business registration certificate displayed or accessible; (4) corporate register and board minute book available on site; (5) working telephone, network connection, and mail-processing station; (6) adequate records of invoicing, receipts, and bank correspondence for at least 5 years; (7) no co-location of more than one unrelated financial entity without partition; (8) a designated person who can respond to tax or registry officials within two hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 10000, as amended), Part IV, Chapter VI, Articles 543 through 613, governing Yuhan Hoesa limited companies, together with the Commercial Registration Act for corporate registration procedures and the Corporate Tax Act for post-registration fiscal obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company (for example, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division), supervised by the Supreme Court of Korea court registration network and accessible through the designated electronic registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (limited company) submitted under the Commercial Registration Act, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. The Korean Commercial Act amendment abolished the former statutory capital floor, so the Articles of Incorporation may fix the capital amount. Each member must fully pay cash contributions or fully perform in-kind contributions before the registration of incorporation. There is no mandatory blocked escrow account, but the competent District Court expects documentary proof of contribution, such as a bank deposit certificate, and the contributed funds may not be released or refunded before the commercial registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY): RESOLVED, that the initial directors and members of Yuhan Hoesa, acting unanimously and in accordance with the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, adopt this resolution as the foundational organizational act of the Company. WHEREAS the Company has been organized as a Yuhan Hoesa limited company for the purpose of non-dilutive revenue-based financing for digital brands and ISIC 6499 royalty financing fund activities, and WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation have been executed and notarized, IT IS RESOLVED as follows. 1. Subscription and Ratification of Capital: The subscription to the issued capital of the Company, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, is hereby ratified, accepted, and confirmed in full. The register of members and contribution schedules are approved as attached, and the managers are instructed to collect, deposit, and verify all capital contributions and to evidence such contributions by bank certificates for submission to the competent District Court. 2. Registered Office: The registered office of the Company is hereby fixed at the address identified in the Articles of Incorporation within the Republic of Korea. The managers are authorized to execute, renew, or terminate any lease, utility, or occupancy documents necessary to maintain that registered office and to notify the Registry, tax authorities, and any relevant bank. 3. Banking Authorization: The managers and the appointed representative are hereby authorized to open, maintain, close, and operate bank accounts in the name of the Company with licensed commercial banks in South Korea, to sign account mandates, electronic banking agreements, wire transfer instructions, direct debit arrangements, and foreign remittance forms, and to provide banks and financial institutions with certified copies of this resolution. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers: [Name] is hereby appointed as the first Representative Director and Manager of the Company, with all authority permitted under the Commercial Act, and [Name] is appointed as first auditor if required by law or the Articles. The officers so appointed are authorized to file the incorporation registration application, obtain certificates of registered matters, corporate seal certificates, business registration certificates, tax identification numbers, and to take all lawful steps necessary for the Company to commence its business. 5. General Authority: The directors and managers are delegated full power to enter into contracts, hire advisers, purchase insurance, and perform any act incidental to the revenue-based financing fund business, subject to the Articles of Incorporation and resolutions of the members. This resolution is effective as of its adoption and continues until revoked by a subsequent valid resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, review, and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and initial capital subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean civil-law notary public in the jurisdiction of the intended registered office, acting under the Notarial Acts Act of the Republic of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft or procure the Articles of Incorporation in English and Korean counterparts, ensuring that all clauses satisfy Article 546 of the Commercial Act, including the corporate name, exact business purpose for ISIC 6499 revenue-based financing and royalty financing fund activities, amount of issued capital, registered office address, names and addresses of initial members, method of contribution, and term of directors or managers. Each subscriber must sign the subscription statement, and the notary must certify the execution and authenticity of the Articles. Any non-cash contribution must be appraised and its performance must be completed before notarization. The notary must refuse certification if the company purpose is unlawful or the capital schedule is ambiguous, so local counsel should review the draft before execution.
required_dossiers: Original Power of Attorney if signed by proxy
Certificate of good standing for corporate members, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a correction request or refuses to certify, cure by amending the Articles and re-executing before the same notary. If an unlawful purpose allegation is raised, narrow the business purpose clause or obtain a formal legal opinion before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of capital and creation of bank evidence of contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed in South Korea by the Financial Supervisory Service, operating within the Bank of Korea payment and settlement framework and bound by Anti-Money Laundering reporting obligations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary subscription account in the name of the incorporator or the company in formation, and transfer each member's entire cash contribution into that dedicated account. Although no statutory minimum capital applies, the capital stated in the Articles must be fully paid by every member. Obtain a bank deposit certificate, paid-in capital statement, or capital verification letter that identifies the Company, the depositor, and the amount of capital. Do not permit withdrawal or refund of the contributed funds before completion of the commercial registration, and do not commingle subscription funds with personal or operational accounts. If any contribution is made in foreign currency, follow Korean foreign exchange transaction reporting and convert the funds into Korean won when required.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit certificate or bank statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account opening owing to incomplete KYC, provide beneficial ownership and identity documentation for all members. If the deposit certificate is delayed, request a written bank confirmation or use another licensed bank and restart the contribution process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the incorporation registration with the competent District Court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office, and electronic filing through the Supreme Court of Korea's court registration information system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation under the Commercial Registration Act using the official court form, together with the notarized Articles, the bank capital deposit certificate, subscription statements, written consents of the initial directors and auditor, and proof of payment of registration taxes and court fees. The court examiner will verify name availability, legality of the business purpose, completeness of capital payment, and acceptance of office by the statutory officers. Upon approval, the company is entered in the commercial register and acquires separate legal personality on that date. After registration, obtain the official certificate of registered matters and the corporate seal certificate from the registry.
required_dossiers: Consent to appointment of directors and auditor
Registration tax and court fee payment receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary request or correction order, file the required materials before the stated deadline. If the application is rejected, cure the deficiency, such as amending the capital statement or obtaining missing consents, and re-file while preserving the paid-in capital deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the business registration certificate and corporate tax identification number from the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered office, with online filing available through the HomeTax electronic service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period generally set at twenty calendar days after court registration, file the business registration application with the National Tax Service. Attach the certificate of registered matters, corporate seal certificate, registered office lease agreement, and identity documents for the representative. State the principal business as non-deposit, non-credit revenue-based financing for digital brands with ISIC 6499 classification and confirm that no physical manufacturing or storage facility is located at the registered office. Once approved, the National Tax Service will issue the Business Registration Certificate containing the corporate tax identification number. This tax number must be used for tax invoices, VAT filings, corporate tax returns, and all banking documentation moving forward.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered matters from the court
Lease agreement for the registered office
Power of attorney for a tax agent, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service demands additional evidence of economic substance, submit the board resolution, lease agreement, and capital contribution proof. If issuance is delayed beyond the service standard, escalate to the local tax office manager or use the HomeTax portal to expedite processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of the first board resolution, opening of operational bank accounts, and completion of governance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General meeting of members and initial directors of Yuhan Hoesa, together with the corporate bank, National Tax Service, and, if triggered, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit for beneficial ownership or AML reporting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first general meeting of members or pass a unanimous written consent approving the First Board Resolution, ratifying the capital subscription, fixing the registered office, appointing the statutory officers, and authorizing bank operations. Execute the formal bank mandate forms and open the operational corporate bank account, using the Certificate of Registered Matters and Business Registration Certificate. Close temporary subscription accounts and transfer the remaining balance into the operational account. Update the internal register of members, issue membership certificates or contribution unit statements, obtain an electronic tax filing certificate, and file any required beneficial ownership or foreign investment report. For the revenue-based financing fund, establish separate ledgers, financing contract registers, AML/CTF policies at the Medium Risk Enhanced level, and segregated accounting from personal or other entity funds.
required_dossiers: Minutes or unanimous written consent of the first meeting
Business registration certificate and tax identification number
Bank account mandate signed by appointed officers
Beneficial ownership and AML filings, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or authority rejects the governance documents, prepare a certified copy of the resolution and an updated officer register. If a beneficial ownership filing is refused, obtain a corrected legal opinion and re-file before disbursing any financing proceeds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing ISIC scope is present in the target business classification.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - ISIC 6499 proprietary non-deposit revenue-based financing and royalty financing fund activities do not trigger a physical operating license in the target formation scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No Environmental Impact Assessment tier is triggered because the company will operate from an office location without a production facility or regulated discharge source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - There are zero wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste, or emission sources attributable to the entity's commercial activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - No Civil Defense fire safety permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval is required beyond the ordinary building occupancy certificate applicable to a professional office. The company must still comply with standard office fire safety and general workplace safety duties under ordinary law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) in South Korea, the entity must first obtain a Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증) from the local district tax office (or via HomeTax). The procedure: (1) Appoint a domestic tax representative (if no permanent establishment in Korea) or a local director; (2) Submit the application form for business registration (including the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, proof of foreign entity existence, and power of attorney for the tax representative) to the competent district tax office; (3) The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) which serves as both the corporate TIN and VAT registration number; (4) For VAT purposes, the entity is automatically registered for VAT upon issuance of the BRN, but must separately file a VAT registration application (사업자등록신청서) if it intends to claim input VAT credits or engage in zero-rated exports; (5) The BRN must be used for all tax filings, e-invoicing, and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box election; Yuhan Hoesa is automatically treated as a corporation for corporate income tax and VAT purposes. However, a foreign entity may elect to be treated as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act if it has a domestic place of business, but this is not a standard election mechanism.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for foreign entities with a domestic place of business; any taxable supply of goods or services in Korea triggers mandatory VAT registration. For domestic small businesses, the annual revenue threshold for mandatory registration is KRW 10 million, but this does not apply to foreign entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices (전자세금계산서) through the HomeTax system for all B2B transactions. The e-invoice must be transmitted to the NTS in real-time via the HomeTax API or the NTS-approved EDI system. For B2C transactions, cash receipts (현금영수증) must be issued and reported. There is no separate fiscal clearance stamping, but the NTS uses real-time data matching to detect discrepancies. Failure to issue e-invoices or cash receipts results in penalties of 1% of the supply value per violation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Article 21 of the VAT Act if the goods are shipped out of Korea and the export is evidenced by customs export declarations. Qualifying offshore digital services (e.g., software, digital content, and royalty income from foreign licensees) are zero-rated if the services are supplied to a non-resident and the consideration is received in foreign currency. The service must be 'used or consumed' outside Korea, and the supplier must retain evidence of the non-resident status of the recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (수출신고필증) issued by Korea Customs Service
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB)
Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank statement evidencing receipt of foreign currency
Contract or agreement with the foreign buyer/licensee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS determines that the export zero-rating was claimed without proper substantiation (e.g., missing FIRC, false export declarations, or failure to repatriate foreign exchange within 180 days), the VAT becomes immediately payable with interest. Penalties include: (1) a 40% penalty on the unpaid VAT amount for fraudulent claims, (2) a 20% penalty for negligent errors, and (3) additional daily interest of 0.025% on the overdue amount. In severe cases, criminal prosecution may be pursued under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, leading to imprisonment up to 5 years or fines up to KRW 50 million. The NTS may also conduct a retrospective audit of up to 5 years and claw back any input VAT credits claimed in connection with the zero-rated supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) operated under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised but strictly supervised foreign exchange regime. The Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods, service fees, royalties and distributable profits, under a simple declaration-based reporting system. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity subscriptions, foreign currency borrowings and outbound investments, generally require bank intermediation or prior declaration through the Foreign Exchange Information System, but do not require routine central bank pre-approval unless they fall under special restrictions such as non-resident won borrowing or real estate acquisitions. The surrender of export proceeds is not mandatory in the form of a forced conversion into won, but all export receivables must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange bank account within the statutory six-month period from the date of export declaration, and any foreign currency held in Korea must remain in accounts maintained at licensed foreign exchange banks. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal after tax clearance, withholding tax certificates and standard foreign exchange bank verification, but dividend or royalty outflows must be supported by board resolutions, audited financial statements and valid tax residence certificates to avoid bonus withholding or interest deduction disallowance. Non-resident convertible debt or quasi-equity inbound instruments need additional reporting under Article 8 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and any use of an offshore fintech aggregator to bypass the domestic banking channel is not recognised for statutory capital verification or tariff/tax refund purposes. Overall, the Korean regime is not a surrender-based or approval-heavy system, but it imposes granular documentary discipline, real end-user validation and strict beneficial ownership identification on every cross-border funding and payment leg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must collect and repatriate all foreign currency export proceeds to a licensed foreign exchange bank in Korea within six months from the date of export declaration; an extension of up to six additional months may be granted by the bank or the Korea Customs Service in justified trade credit circumstances. There is no fixed percentage of export proceeds that must be compulsorily converted into Korean won, but any conversion, sale or transfer of the foreign currency must be executed through a licensed domestic bank and reported in FEIS with the appropriate trade settlement classification code. If the export claim is partially unpaid or the receivable is written off, the exporter must file a trade settlement delay or non-collection report, otherwise the bank may suspend subsequent settlements and report the matter to the National Tax Service and the Financial Supervisory Service.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD dual sub-ledger)
Foreign Currency Current Account for Trade Proceeds and Basic Operational KRW Account
Corporate Settlement Account with Royalty/Trade Purpose Code Setup
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account with Foreign Exchange Forward Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI providers have a Low viability rating for primary treasury operations in South Korea. They are not licensed by the Financial Services Commission to open domestic won-denominated settlement accounts, cannot access the FEIS foreign exchange reporting network, and are not eligible counterparties for mandatory export collection or statutory trade settlement verification. A foreign-owned Korean LLC must maintain a physical account relationship with a domestic Tier-1 bank for all inbound capital subscription wiring, trade settlement, VAT refunds and tax payments. Offshore EMIs may be used only as supplementary payment sensors for non-Korean e-commerce routing, but they cannot serve as the main treasury rail or as the bank of record for corporate verification, and the regulator will treat any attempt to route royalty inflows through an EMI without a domestic FEIS report as a potential violation of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and ultimate beneficial owners with an ownership threshold of 20% or more must appear physically in-branch for the KYC identity verification and transaction-pattern interview at the Korean Tier-1 bank. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for a non-resident corporate client, although some banks allow a remote video KYC interview for the foreign director if a Korean-resident signatory with a valid Alien Registration Card or national ID attends in person to deposit the corporate resolution and execute the account opening agreement. In all cases the bank requires a wet-ink or legally certified board resolution designating the account signatories, the original apostilled certificate of incorporation and articles of incorporation, and a current personal identification document of each signatory and beneficial owner. Without a physical visit by at least one authorised principal or a qualified Korean resident agent, the bank's compliance committee will reject the account application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership layers involving foreign trusts, nominee shareholdings or private holding companies that obscure the natural persons behind the Korean LLC, which is a classic red flag for shell-company financing structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete beneficial ownership chart with each intermediate entity's certificate of incorporation, share register, valid passport copies of all natural persons holding more than 10% of the economic interest, notarised and apostilled declaration of source of wealth, six months of bank statements from the legal owner of the inbound funds, and a signed obligation letter allowing the Korean bank to request further corporate records from any offshore holding entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-based financing and royalty financing fund activity is classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced because the commercial operation involves recurring digital content royalty inflows from gaming, streaming and e-commerce brands, which may be considered an unusual prepayment or receivables monetisation pattern by AML underwriting teams.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An external audit report for the last two fiscal years, certified royalty and revenue financing agreements, a list of all material licensors and payers, a projected monthly cash-flow waterfall, the underlying digital brand contracts that justify the royalty stream, completed source-of-funds questionnaires, and a detailed business narrative describing how the financing fund acquires rights and receives non-dilutive repayments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and trade embargo exposure from cross-border digital revenue flows that can originate from a geographically diverse set of unknown end-users, including possible payments from sanctioned jurisdictions or from persons using virtual private network masked IP addresses to access Korean digital content.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A live OFAC/EU/UN and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions screening report generated within 30 days of account opening, the company's customer geolocation and IP screening policy, proof of comprehensive transaction monitoring procedures, a negative news investigation report for every beneficial owner and counterparty, and a written undertaking that the bank will be given read-only access to the company's payment gateway so that transaction-level screening continues on a real-time basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory director and signatory are not resident in Korea and attempt to rely on a power of attorney or proxy to open the account, which triggers heightened verification and anti-impersonation concerns under Korean bank KYC regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A board resolution explicitly authorising the Korean resident signatory, a notarised and apostilled power of attorney limited to account operation, the Korean signatory's valid Alien Registration Card or Korean ID card proof of address, a direct video interview with the non-resident director at the time of account opening, and a written declaration that the Korean signatory is not a nominee for money laundering, with all bank-issued tokens and OTP devices requiring biometric activation in the Korean branch.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be wired by the foreign shareholder using SWIFT MT103 to the Korean LLC's capital escrow account maintained at a Tier-1 domestic bank, with the remitter name matching the equity investor's name stated in the board resolution and shareholder registry. The purpose of payment must reference the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act capital transaction code, typically code 62001 for inbound equity capital or code 62002 for non-resident loan/deposit, and the Korean receiving bank will prepare the FEIS foreign exchange purchase/settlement declaration. For a domestic limited liability company, there is no minimum paid-in capital amount, but the bank will require a capital verification certificate or accountant's confirmation letter if the inbound funds are to be treated as subscribed capital for entity registration and tax purposes. The bank will block or return inflows where the source is a personal account of an unrelated third party or where the originator is a shell entity without a clear economic link to the Korean operating company, and the funds must not mix with capital of other group companies. Inbound royalty financing proceeds intended for onward lending or distribution must be separately classified as debt/non-equity financing in the FEIS system, and the tax withholding obligations on imputed interest or royalties must be settled before outbound remittance is approved.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for royalty payments, revenue-sharing distributions, trade services and operational expenses must be executed through the domestic Korean clearing rails using SWIFT MT103 for direct cash disbursements, or commercial letters of credit and documentary collections for structured merchandise trade. The beneficiary bank and intermediary bank must be cleared through the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication network; payments to non-bank EMIs are treated as unusual and require additional KYC evidence. For all outbound foreign currency payments above the equivalent of USD 50,000, the Korean bank will submit a FEIS transaction report with the appropriate payment purpose code, and the company must present an underlying trade contract, invoice, tax withholding certificate, board resolution and beneficial ownership declaration. For same-won cross-border disbursements, the Korea Financial Telecommunications & Clearing Institute (KFTC) and the KRW-CDP settlement system are used for domestic legs, while the final cross-border leg will be settled in USD or KRW through the correspondent banking network of the local Tier-1 bank. The use of commercial LC and documentary collections is permissible for physical goods and software licensing only when the underlying trade documents are verifiable, and any receivable discounting or factoring of future royalty income must be separately approved by the bank's credit department because it creates contingent liquidity exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD deliverable forward contracts with real underlying exposure including royalty inflows and outbound financing principal, provided the maturity matches the commercial cash-flow timing and the contract is transacted with a registered Korean foreign exchange bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore or with a domestic bank for hedging non-KRW foreign currency cash flows, subject to strict documentation of the underlying receivable and a prohibition on speculative naked positioning

Cross-currency swaps between KRW and USD or KRW and EUR for the purpose of matching long-dated royalty financing assets with funding liabilities, supported by board-approved treasury policy and real transaction identifiers

Currency options and structured collars are not permitted in the initial treasury stage without special regulatory approval; only plain-vanilla forwards and cross-currency interest-rate swaps are considered permissible by the bank compliance committee for a medium-risk royalty financing fund

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and financial statements filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end (31 March for a 31 December fiscal year); electronic filing extensions may apply as provided under the Corporate Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unfiled or fraudulent return attracts an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax (10% for negligent non-filing), plus daily delinquency interest at 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% annually) from the original due date; persistent non-filing for three consecutive years allows the NTS to declare the company dormant and the Registration Court may administratively strike off the entity after a 14-day public notice under Article 520-2 of the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local income tax return on corporate income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si/Gun/Gu) via unified filing with the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax return; 31 March for calendar-year entities, extended to the next business day if a holiday
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting triggers additional taxes equivalent to 20% of the deficient amount (or 10% for unintentional errors) plus delinquency interest of 0.022% per day; continuous non-payment can lead to seizure of bank accounts and other assets by the local government.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report submission to the supervisory authority if statutory size thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The auditor's report must be delivered to the FSS within 30 days after approval by the equity holders' meeting, and such meeting must be held within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (no later than 30 June for a calendar-year entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit an audit report or submission of a materially false report exposes the company to an administrative fine of up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 38,000), criminal fines or imprisonment for responsible officers, and in serious cases the audit opinion may be reported as adverse, which can trigger regulatory inspection and judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership annual confirmation and change report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual written confirmation of beneficial owners must be completed and retained by 31 March each year; any reportable change in the ownership structure, including a transfer of membership interest exceeding 10% of the equity, must be filed with KoFIU within 30 calendar days of the relevant event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing may result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 30 million (approximately USD 23,000) and, for willful false reporting, criminal penalties under Article 8 of the Financial Transaction Reports Act, including imprisonment of up to 3 years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily subject to independent certified audit for a fiscal year if, at the close of the immediately preceding fiscal year, (i) total assets are KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.1 million) or more; or (ii) the company is deemed a publicly held corporation under the Act on External Audit of Corporations; or (iii) the company falls under specified financial sectors and total revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion (approximately USD 76 million), or headcount reaches 500 or more, as the FSS may designate. For non-audited small companies, a Korean CPA may still be required to deliver a review report under tax filings if the entity's paid-in capital exceeds KRW 500 million (approximately USD 385,000).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) is mandatory for audited entities; private non-listed SMEs may elect the Korean GAAP for non-public companies (K-GAAP) or K-IFRS for Small and Medium Enterprises (K-IFRS for SMEs), all approved by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (FTRA) and the Korean Commercial Act, the Yuhan Hoesa must conduct a real-name and beneficial-ownership verification at each business relationship opening and on an annual calendar-year basis. The written confirmation must state the name, date of birth, nationality, and percentage of equity ownership of each ultimate beneficial owner, must be signed by the representative director by 31 March, and must be retained for at least 7 years. Any transfer of membership interest that changes the beneficiary owners or that increases an owner to a controlling level (10% or more) must be reported to KoFIU within 30 calendar days and be reflected in the company's member register before the year-end confirmation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 1,800 per year for a professional registered office and compliance agent in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 25,000 for a mandatory statutory audit of a small-to-mid-sized Korean LLC; if exempt, a CPA review for tax nexus purposes typically costs USD 2,000 - USD 6,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% (plus 10% local income tax surtax on corporate income tax, producing a 24.2% top effective marginal rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea does not maintain a general patent box, but preferential regimes exist for Free Economic Zone operators (100% exemption for 3 to 5 years and 50% reduction for 2 years), qualifying R&D expenditure (tax credits of up to 25%), and foreign-invested high-tech enterprise incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act. A Yuhan Hoesa engaging in royalty financing may also access venture-fund tax deferrals or capital-gains relief, but only where the Korean entity performs real investment management functions and the royalty assets remain Korean-source for CIT purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 10) plus supporting schedules; electronically filed through the National Tax Service Hometax portal (홈택스) using the Korean business registration number and non-resident OID identification where applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly advance corporate income tax payments during the fiscal year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (Article 60, Corporate Tax Act). A non-resident corporation with a Korean permanent establishment or Korean-source income uses the same annual deadline, unless extended by a Government-approved special circumstance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identity and fiscal-year data, including entity legal name, Korean business registration number, address, representative director, and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Yuhan Hoesa must disclose all non-resident shareholders and foreign-director particulars in the shareholder and representative director schedules. Use English transliteration of non-resident names and country codes to permit accurate DTA treaty matching. Failure to disclose a foreign parent entity may trigger the formal request for correction under Articles 36 to 40 of the Framework Act on National Taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement listing gross revenue, royalty income, financing fees, interest income, intercompany expenses, operating expenditure, and net book income before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border royalties paid to non-residents must be separately disclosed and reconciled with the withholding-tax schedule. Under the arm's length principle, royalty expenses payable to a foreign related party are deductible only to the extent of the amount an independent lender would have charged for the same risk; excess portions are to be added back in Box 3 and flagged to the transfer-pricing unit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of book income to taxable income; includes non-deductible provisions, disallowed entertainment expenses, capital gains adjustments, and intercompany pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled entities should attach an intercompany pricing adjustment schedule reflecting any CUP or TNMM benchmarking exercise. If the fund has issued a financing royal and receives premium fees, allocate the Korean source portion accurately; transfer pricing audit risk is high for entities under the ISIC 6499 non-dilutive royalty/financing fund business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income calculation after applying losses carried forward, exemptions, deductions, and special tax concessions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is limited to a maximum of 5 fiscal years from the loss year (as specified in the schema). The NTS will require the prior-year returns, ownership continuity schedules, and evidence that the Korean business has economic substance. A resident-less shell holding a royalty fund will not be allowed to offset Korean-source royalty income with foreign losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computation using the statutory progressive structure and the local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the applicable progressive rates for the fiscal year: 10% on taxable income not exceeding KRW 200 million, 20% on the next band up to KRW 20 billion, and 22% on amounts exceeding KRW 20 billion. In addition, compute 10% of the corporate income tax as local income tax surtax; the total must be disclosed as a separate line in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of foreign-source income and foreign taxes paid; calculation of the foreign tax credit limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean-resident Yuhan Hoesa, foreign-source earnings streaming from royalty contracts must be supported by invoices and tax vouchers. Non-resident shareholders cannot use this box to claim Korean foreign tax credit; instead they must use the DTA relief path via the withholding agent. The NTS may re-characterise any attempt to claim foreign tax credit as a dividend distribution if the underlying arrangement fails an economic substance analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax reconciliation for outbound dividends, interest, royalties, and other Korean-source payments to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the gross remittance amount, the statutory withholding rate (20% plus 2% local surtax), the treaty rate claimed, and the Tax Residency Certificate reference number. If the beneficial owner is a individual or fund under a low-tax jurisdiction, attach a beneficial-ownership statement and a detailed DTA position paper. Overcast treaty relief can be challenged within 3 years of assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 10 without an approved extension results in an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax; after 6 months the additional tax rises to 30%. Under-reporting triggers a negligence additional tax of 10% of the underreported amount, which is increased to 20% where under-reporting is due to a so-called 'improper rebate' or gross negligence. Daily overdue interest accrues at 0.03% on the unpaid principal from the day following the statutory due date until payment. Intentional false declarations constitute criminal tax evasion under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Punishment of Tax Evanis Act, punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to 5 times the amount of tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on the gross dividend amount payable to a non-resident corporate shareholder, plus a 2% local income tax surtax calculated on the 20% base, producing an aggregate 22% withholding on outbound dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of its country of residence, dated within the same calendar year as the payment, and containing the beneficial owner's name, address, tax identification number, and period of tax residence. That owner must then submit the TRC together with a beneficial-ownership statement (Form 13-2, Application for Non-Resident Tax Reduction or Exemption under a Double Tax Treaty) to the Korean withholding agent before the payment due date, or alternatively before the end of the withholding month. The Korean company must retain the TRC, contract, and invoice trail in its records for at least 5 years. If the treaty-reduced rate is not applied at source, the non-resident may file a refund claim with the NTS within the 3-year statutory period, attaching the TRC and evidencing that the Korean payer had no reason to disbelieve beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for royalties is 20% plus 2% local surtax (22%); statutory rate for interest paid to non-residents is likewise 20% plus 2% local surtax (22%). Korean tax treaties vary by partner: interest is commonly reduced to 0% or 10% and royalties to 0%, 10% or 15%. Any reduced treaty rate must be matched to the specific DTA article and a Limitation of Benefits clause should be counter-signed by the beneficial owner; otherwise the statutory 22% applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 billion in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions per fiscal year for mandatory Local File and Master File; Country-by-Country Report is due where the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue is at least KRW 2.5 trillion, and the Korean entity receives a CbC notification.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not employ the Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulation, but its substance-over-form doctrine, the OECD BEPS Main Purpose Test, and the Danish beneficial-owner jurisprudence operate identically. A Yuhan Hoesa engaged in royalty financing must evidence Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) performed in Korea, namely strategic asset acquisition, credit and market risk decision-making, negotiation of royalty and financing contracts, ongoing portfolio monitoring, treasury and liquidity management, and board-level assumption of risk. If the entity is merely a conduit receiving Korean royalties and passing dividends to foreign investors without staff, premises and meeting record, Korean tax authorities will not only deny treaty benefits but also ignore the legal form under the Abuse of Legal Entity doctrine, imposing corporate tax at the full 22% rate plus local surtax and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident controlled Yuhan Hoesa is incorporated to collect royalties for digital content or branding and immediately remits profits as royalties or dividends to a foreign parent. The entity has no employees, no office lease, no negotiations, no board minutes and no retained risk, and the sole purpose of the structure is to avoid Korean corporate income tax and to claim treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will disregard the corporate entity under Article 23 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Article 43 of the Corporate Tax Act. The royalty income is re-characterised as Korean-source dividend actually attributable to a permanent establishment, resulting in a 22% withholding assessment on the full remitted amount, plus a 40% negligence penalty for gross intentional underreporting, plus daily overdue interest at 0.03%, and rejection of the treaty claim under the Principal Purpose Test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Creditors and the National Tax Service may pierce the corporate veil under the Korean Commercial Act and Civil Act joint liability rules. Directors, shadow directors, and de facto managers are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate income taxes, the 40% negligence penalty, and collection charges. Criminal referral is mandatory when intentional evasion exceeds KRW 300 million; the responsible director faces imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to 5 times the tax evaded. The Ministry of Economy and Finance places the director on the immigration departure prohibition (blacklist) until the entire tax delinquency is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa enters into a royalty financing arrangement with a foreign affiliate under an inflated royalty rate, excessive interest rate, or structurally non-arm's-length covenant under the revenue-based financing model, reducing Korean taxable income by shifting profit to a zero or low tax jurisdiction, and omitting the mandatory Local File/Master File and international transaction statement despite cross-border intercompany transactions exceeding the KRW 50 billion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS adjusts the transaction under Articles 88 and 89 of the Corporate Tax Act. The excessive deduction is added back to taxable income, re-computation of CIT and local surtax is made, a transfer pricing additional tax of 10% (or 20% for serious non-disclosure) is applied under Article 167-3, and a 0.03% daily overdue interest applies from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director who signs the false return is jointly liable for the adjusted tax, penalties and interest. Where the transfer-pricing scheme is criminal, the director is exposed to imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to 5 times the avoided tax. In the recovery phase, the NTS attaches the director's personal bank accounts, vehicles, and real estate; unresolved delinquency above KRW 500 million also imposes a travel ban and blacklisting of the director and the company's ultimate beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Non-Compliance and Unlawful Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity pays outbound dividends, interest, or royalty payments to a non-resident beneficial owner without withholding the 22% statutory aggregate amount, ignoring the DTA reduction or application deadlines, failing to secure the TRC and beneficial ownership evidence, or structuring remittances as consultancy fees or refunds to circumvent the withholding regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is liable for the unwithheld tax and additional tax of 10% of the unwithheld amount (or 20% of the unremitted amount if collected but not paid), plus 0.03% daily overdue interest. The NTS may assess the representative as the withholding taxpayer under the joint liability doctrine. Criminal prosecution for embezzlement or unlawful non-remission results in a fine up to KRW 50 million and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and the finance director become personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax and penalties, and the NTS can execute immediately against personal assets. If the amount unpaid is especially high, the directors are registered on the immigration departure restriction (blacklist) and cannot leave Korea without posting a bond or providing a tax clearance certificate. Repeated infringement also triggers disqualification management under the Commercial Act and leads to revocation of visas of foreign directors, with expulsion from Korea.
